title: Matching Game: A Colorful Memory Challenge
author: Jason Lamb
excerpt: A child-friendly browser memory game with colors, letters, numbers, objects, adjustable grids, and optional spoken tiles.

cover.alt: Matching Game desktop interface showing a colorful grid of face-down tiles

content_html:
Matching Game gives young players a simple memory challenge. Choose Colors, Letters, Numbers, or Objects, then turn over two tiles at a time. A pair stays visible, while a mismatch turns back after a short pause.

The board can be changed from a compact 2-by-2 grid up to 6-by-6, with an even number of tiles in every layout. The timer starts on the first reveal and stops when all pairs are found. Attempts, completed rounds, pairs, and best times are kept for the current browser tab session, so children can play without creating an account.

Tiles can also be read aloud. The game uses supplied recordings when available and falls back to the browser voice for missing files. Optional signed-in history saves completed game summaries, while card order and moves stay on the device.

Desktop and mobile play

The layout keeps the tile grid touch friendly on smaller screens and gives the game controls room on desktop.
